text: His name was Babur, and at Panapat, north of Delhi, he faced the Sultan Ibrahim Lodi,
who had a far bigger army and around a hundred elephants.
But Babur brought something new to India.
Cannons and guns.
The elephants panicked.
In a single day, the Sultanate was gone.
Babur founded the Mughal Empire.
Stitch, again.
He also wrote a remarkable memoir, The Babur Nama, and honestly, he wasn't that impressed
with India.
He complained there were no good horses, no good grapes, and no good melons.
Your Majesty, the finest mangoes in Hindustan.
No melons?
Mangoes, Majesty, everyone loves them.
Day 400, still no melons.
Babur ruled for only four years.
His son Humayun lost the whole empire to an Afghan general, Sher Shah Suri.
Sher Shah ruled for just five years, but he was brilliant.
He improved the Great Road from Bengal to the northwest, later called the Grand Trunk
Road, with rest houses and wells along the way.
And he issued a new silver coin.
He called it the Rupiah.
Just holding up a coin?
The Rupiah started by the guy who kicked the moogles out.
